title: [13/6/2024] Percentages of different types of household waste recycled
prompt: The chart below shows the percentages of different types of household waste that were recycled in one city between 1992 and 2002. Summarise the information by selecting and reporting the main features, and make comparisons where relevant.

frame.name: Introduction
paragraphs: The bar chart presents information about the recycling rates of four categories of household waste in one city between 1992 and 2002.

frame.name: Overview
paragraphs: Overall, there was an upward trend in recycling rates across all categories during the period shown. In addition, glass became the most recycled material by 2002, whereas plastic consistently had the lowest recycling rates throughout the years.

frame.name: Body 1
paragraphs: Regarding the most recycled materials, in 1992, approximately 20% of glass waste was recycled, which was slightly higher than the figure for paper, at around 18%. Thereafter, the recycling rate of glass waste saw a substantial increase, rising to about 30% in 1997 before surging dramatically to nearly 48% by 2002. Similarly, paper recycling grew steadily, reaching roughly 32% in 1997 and climbing further to about 38% by the end of the period.

frame.name: Body 2
paragraphs: As for the remaining categories, in 1992, cans were recycled at a rate of 18%, while the figure for plastic was considerably lower at 10%. Subsequently, the recycling of cans experienced some fluctuations, dropping to 14% in 1997 before recovering strongly to reach 24% by 2002. In contrast, plastic recycling showed minimal improvement over the decade, with its rate increasing slightly to 12% in 1997 and remaining at this level by the end of the period.
